workflow.device: Explicit device wins; otherwise current/default device for top-level factories, prototype device for new_*. CPU pinned allocation is a separate transfer/lifetime class. Never count Meta symbolic execution or MPS host fallback as native execution.
workflow.gradient: Factory requires_grad defaults False; True is legal only for floating/complex output dtypes. Creation of a new leaf is distinct from differentiable dependence on input data/endpoints. no_grad has a factory-function exception; inference_mode and forward-mode need distinct classes.
workflow.out: Out overloads mutate supplied tensor and return it. Preserve object/storage identity, correct-shape strides and source/destination dtype/device rules. Wrong-shape resize/deprecation behavior is operator-specific. out with gradients needed is unsupported; do not infer correctness from global out notes.

analytical_acceptance: Assert metadata, storage extent/alias lifetime and computed values only after writing all initialized elements.
For strided shapes calculate address map and overlap; invalid stride tuple lengths/negative strides and allocation overflow reject.
Deterministic algorithms+fill-uninitialized controls require source-defined NaN/maxinteger values; ordinary uninitialized data is never compared to arbitrary reference bytes.

records.semantics: Retained legacy documented capability: Tensor(Tensor) aliases and tracks autograd; sequence input coerces to default floating dtype even for all integers; torch.Size and integer-size constructor forms allocate uninitialized storage. This is not equivalent to torch.tensor or new_tensor.
reference_contradictions: Tensor constructor documentation says dtype/device cannot be explicitly specified but also lists a device keyword; manual parser accepts device for some overloads and forbids it for Tensor alias form. Preserve overload-specific contracts.
acceptance: Tensor(sourceTensor) alias/storage/autograd propagation vs tensor(sourceTensor) detached copy.
Tensor([1,2]) default floating vs tensor([1,2]) int64; Tensor(Size([2,3])) allocation vs Tensor([2,3]) two data elements.
